correctness.rationale: The finite theorem reduces to exact enumeration of all unordered pairs of odd primes p<=floor(2^(3m/4)); the exact cutoff is computed as isqrt(isqrt(2^(3m))). A complete Eratosthenes sieve and pair-product bitset indexed by all 2^(m-1) odd unit classes proves both coverage and noncoverage for EVERY integer m in [1,21], not a sample. Independent implementation reconstructed all 21 missing-count values (1,2,3,3,5,11,17,30,54,70,121,162,190,240,216,183,92,42,7,3,0), verifying the first complete case m=21 and that m=20 has precisely three unrepresented residues 122299,333455,414971. At m=21, full coverage first occurs at prime cutoff 50923, with prior prime 50909 and last obstruction 745135, represented by 50923*7757 modulo 2^21. Independent modular-inverse obstruction reconfirmed that no earlier prime cutoff represents this last residue. This proves only the finite interval and no perpetuation for m>21.

value.rationale: The exponent 3/4 is a mathematically motivated critical boundary of prime-product covering in a recent random model, not a hand-picked computational ratio. The first sharp dyadic full coverage at that endpoint and adjacent three-hole failure provide an exact and reproducible benchmark for an important open covering problem. A meaningful finite sharp cutoff does not require proving an infinite theorem.

limitations: Finite m<=21 theorem only; neither any m>21 nor general EOS conjecture proved.
